title: New Shoes
summary: Making a practical choice can lead to a happy reward.
content:
Mom looked down at Ben’s feet. “Your shoes have holes. It’s time to buy new shoes,” she said.

She took Ben to the shoe store. Ben tried on many different shoes. He tried on brown ones and green ones, blue ones and black ones. In the end, they bought the green ones.

“You did a good job buying shoes,” said Mom. “For a treat, let’s stop at the beach.”

“Yay!” said Ben. “I will go barefoot!”

vocabulary.meaning: put on to check the fit

activities.language_notice: “It’s time to + verb” is used to say that an action should happen now.

title: One Little Seed, One Big Tree
summary: Small beginnings can grow into something big.
content:
Kate really likes apples. She asks her teacher, “Where do apples come from?”

“Apples grow on apple trees,” says her teacher.

“Where do apple trees come from?” Kate asks again.

“Apple trees come from apple seeds. Inside an apple, there are many little seeds. Each seed can grow into an apple tree,” her teacher says.

Wow! From this little seed, a big apple tree will grow!

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Small beginnings can grow into something big.

What can each apple seed become?

short_answer: What fruit does Kate like?
Where do apples grow?

vocabulary.meaning: the small part of a plant that can grow

activities.language_notice: Questions with “Where do … come from?” ask about origin.

title: Grandma’s Cake
summary: Unexpected accidents can become funny family memories.
content:
On Saturday, I was helping Grandma bake a cake. While I was mixing, her cat jumped right into the bowl!

Everything spilled all over us. When we finally cleaned it all up, we couldn’t find the cat! Where had she gone?

There she was! She was lying on the floor while Grandma’s dog licked her clean.

The dog got more cake than we did!

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Unexpected accidents can become funny family memories.

What happened to the mixture?

The dog jumped into the bowl.

The family ate more cake than the dog.
short_answer: What jumped into the bowl?
What happened to the mixture?
How did the cat get clean?

vocabulary.meaning: to cook food in an oven

activities.language_notice: “While + past continuous” describes an action in progress when another action happened.

title: Our Changing Teeth–1
summary: Our first teeth grow in a predictable order and are temporary.
content:
Do you know that our teeth are changing as we grow?

Around the age of eight months, our first teeth begin to grow.

The middle teeth in the front of our mouth come first. Then, the teeth at the sides. And finally, the ones at the very back of the mouth.

There are 20 teeth in total. These teeth are called baby teeth. But these teeth won’t be with us for long.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Our first teeth grow in a predictable order and are temporary.

questions.prompt: When do first teeth begin to grow?
Which teeth usually come first?
How many baby teeth are there in total?

short_answer: When do first teeth begin to grow?
Which teeth usually come first?
How many baby teeth are there in total?

vocabulary.meaning: hard parts in the mouth used for biting

activities.language_notice: Sequence words “first,” “then,” and “finally” show the order of events.

title: Our Changing Teeth–2
summary: Adult teeth must be cared for because they are meant to last a lifetime.
content:
By the time we reach the age of seven, our baby teeth begin to fall out.

First, the front middle teeth fall out. Then the teeth on the side, and finally the teeth at the back of our mouth.

Don’t worry though. As our baby teeth fall out, new teeth grow to take their place. By our late teens, we will have all 32 of our adult teeth.

But unlike our baby teeth, the adult teeth will be with us for the rest of our lives. That’s why it’s important to take care of these teeth. They are the last ones we will ever get.

options: Adult teeth must be cared for because they are meant to last a lifetime.

Adult teeth do not need care.
short_answer: Around what age do baby teeth begin to fall out?
What replaces baby teeth?
How many adult teeth do we have by our late teens?

activities.language_notice: “By the time” connects a time point with something completed or happening by then.

title: Purple Mountains–1
summary: Curiosity encourages us to look more closely and learn.
content:
Josh’s family lives near the mountains. In the fall, the mountains look beautiful.

“Look, Dad! Those mountains are purple!” says Josh.

His dad laughs. “They’re not really purple.”

Josh is puzzled. He scratches his head and asks, “Then why do they look purple?”

His dad says, “Because we’re far away. Come! I’ll show you.”

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Curiosity encourages us to look more closely and learn.

short_answer: Where does Josh’s family live?

Why is Josh puzzled?
short_answer_keys: The mountains look purple but are not really purple.

vocabulary.meaning: a colour made from red and blue

activities.language_notice: “Why do they look …?” asks for the reason behind an appearance.

title: Purple Mountains–2
summary: Distance and light can change how colours appear.
content:
“Get in the car,” says Josh’s dad. “Let’s go to the mountains.”

They drive to the mountains. As they get closer, they see that the mountains are not purple anymore.

“Oh, I see,” says Josh. “But why?”

“From far away, the light scatters, making the mountains look purple,” says his dad.

“Cool,” says Josh. “Let’s drive home and make them purple again!”

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Distance and light can change how colours appear.

What happens as they get closer?
options: The mountains no longer look purple.

true_false: Josh and Dad go toward the mountains.

Josh wants to stay at the mountain forever.
short_answer: How do Josh and Dad travel?
What happens as they get closer?
What makes distant mountains look purple?
short_answer_keys: The mountains no longer look purple.

vocabulary.meaning: now or from now on, usually in negatives

activities.language_notice: “As they get closer” shows two changes happening at the same time.

title: Pumpkins for Sale
summary: Honesty allows people in a community to trust one another.
content:
October 31st was coming soon. While my mom was driving home, she saw many pumpkins on the road side.

No one was there, just a sign. It said: Pumpkins for sale. Large $10. Small $5.

My mom stopped the car. She took two large pumpkins. As she put the money in the basket, she saw many twenty-dollar bills inside.

“Isn’t it nice that people can still trust each other like this?” Mom said to me.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Honesty allows people in a community to trust one another.

questions.prompt: What holiday date was coming soon?
How much did a large pumpkin cost?
How many large pumpkins did Mom take?

A seller stood beside the pumpkins.
Mom put money in a basket.
The basket was empty.
short_answer: What holiday date was coming soon?
How much did a large pumpkin cost?
How many large pumpkins did Mom take?
activities.language_notice: “While” and “as” can introduce actions happening at the same time.

title: The Red Plant
summary: Patient, consistent care can bring about change.
content:
Adam gave his mom a special plant. It had red leaves. But after a few months, the leaves became green.

“How can we make the plant red again?” he asked.

“It takes some time, but it’s easy,” said his mom.

During the day, they put the plant in sunlight. At night, they covered it with a box. They did this for two months.

Soon, the plant was red again.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Patient, consistent care can bring about change.

Where did they put the plant during the day?
How long did they follow the routine?

The plant stayed green forever.
short_answer: What colour were the leaves at first?

vocabulary.meaning: different in a good or important way

a repeated way of doing things

activities.language_notice: Time expressions “during the day” and “at night” contrast two routines.

title: A Ballet Dancer
summary: Practice helps us perform confidently even when we feel nervous.
content:
Cora is a ballet dancer. Every week, she takes lessons with Miss Martha, learning the positions, steps, and movements.

Her grandma’s 100th birthday is coming. On that day, Cora will dance for her grandma, and other family and friends.

She is nervous, but she has been practising. She dances nicely. Her friends and family stand and cheer for her after she finishes!

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?

short_answer: What kind of dancer is Cora?
Whose birthday is being celebrated?
How old is Grandma turning?

vocabulary.meaning: set ways of holding the body

activities.language_notice: The present perfect continuous “has been practising” describes an action continuing up to now.

title: Orange-Fish
summary: Names may come from history rather than a literal appearance.
content:
Melissa bought a fish. “You’re my favourite orange-fish,” she said.

“He is a goldfish,” said her brother Jimmy.

“But look, he’s orange coloured, not gold,” she said.

“That doesn’t matter,” said Jimmy. “A long time ago, silver carp turned yellowish-orange, and people called them goldfish.”

“Well, he is an orange-fish to me,” said Melissa.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Names may come from history rather than a literal appearance.

short_answer: What pet did Melissa buy?

What colour does Melissa say the fish is?

vocabulary.meaning: a small pet fish, often orange

title: A Party for Parents
summary: Thoughtful creativity can make a celebration special.
content:
“Today is a special day for Mom and Dad,” said Nick. “Let’s throw a party for them,” said Sara.

They put balloons in the family room. They wanted to make a cake, but their parents were in the kitchen. So they drew a picture of a cake.

They invited their brother, sister, and grandma to the party.

When their parents entered the family room, they yelled, “Happy Anniversary!”

What a surprise!

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Thoughtful creativity can make a celebration special.

questions.prompt: Who suggests throwing a party?
Why do the children draw a cake?
options: Their parents are in the kitchen.

The parents plan the surprise.

short_answer_keys: Their parents are in the kitchen.

vocabulary.meaning: rubber bags filled with air or gas

title: National Park
summary: National Parks protect nature while allowing people to enjoy it.
content:
Henry lives near a National Park. That is a special type of park.

National Parks are usually very large pieces of land. The land is chosen to protect its beauty, plants, and animals. But National Parks are for people to enjoy too.

One day, Henry hopes to work in a National Park. He wants to help protect the land for everyone.

Why is National Park land chosen?

vocabulary.meaning: protected land for nature and people

title: Going Too Fast–1
summary: Excitement can grow quickly when an activity speeds up.
content:
On a cold, snowy winter day, Charlie and his father wanted to have some fun.

They took their snowboard to the hill and set it down at the top.

“Ready?” asked Charlie. “Here we go!” said his father.

The snowboard carrying them began to go down the hill. It was slow at the beginning, then it was going faster and faster.

“Here we come!” Charlie was excited.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Excitement can grow quickly when an activity speeds up.

short_answer: What is the weather like?

vocabulary.meaning: with snow falling or on the ground

title: Going Too Fast–2
summary: Fun activities still require care and attention to safety.
content:
When Charlie’s father found the board was going too fast, he tried to slow it down, but it was too late.

In a few seconds, they flew off the board and hit the tree at the bottom of the hill.

“Ouch!” his father cried. “I think I broke my ankle!”

Charlie started to cry. His father said, “I’m okay. Let’s go to the hospital.”

He smiled and said, “We had fun today, didn’t we?”

options: Fun activities still require care and attention to safety.

title: Clean Room
summary: Cleaning and persistence can help us find what seems lost.
content:
Abe couldn’t find his favourite toy car. “If you clean up your bedroom, you might find it,” his mom said.

Abe put away his clothes, books, and toys. He found his toy truck and dirt bike. But he didn’t find his toy car.

Feeling sad, he lay on his bed. Then, he felt something underneath. It was his toy car!

title: The Happy Pumpkin
summary: It is good to express your own creative ideas.
content:
For many years, my brothers and I visited a farm and picked pumpkins for Halloween.

My brothers wanted to carve scary pumpkins with sharp teeth and angry eyes, but not me. I wanted my pumpkin to be different and special.

I carved a laughing pumpkin with a friendly smile and kind eyes. It was my happy pumpkin.

title: Coco the Bird–1
summary: Dreams may begin to come true through unexpected opportunities.
content:
Coco the bird lived in a pet store, waiting for someone to buy him.

“Someday, I’ll sail the seas on a pirate’s ship,” he said.

“That’s awesome,” said Max the puppy.

One day, a lady came into the store. “I’d like a special pet,” she said.

“This bird likes the water,” said the owner.

“I’ll buy him,” she said and took him home.

title: Coco the Bird–2
summary: Imagination and friendship can turn disappointment into fun.
content:
Coco stared at the lady’s pool, wishing he could sail the high seas. “I guess the pirate’s life is not for me.” Ding Dong.

“Welcome, Peter,” said his Grandma. “Meet Coco, my new pet bird.”

“Cool,” said Peter. He put Coco on his shoulder and said, “I’m Pirate Peter!”

All day, they swam in the pool, pretending to sail the seas and fly the pirate flag.

title: Grandma’s Old Pot
summary: Useful objects deserve care, gratitude, and less waste.
content:
Grandma has an old cooking pot. Over the years, she has made so many wonderful meals for us with that pot.

Now, that pot is too old. We told Grandma to throw it away. But she said, “No. It’s still usable. If I throw it away, it will just be trash.”

For Christmas, we sent her a new pot as a gift. Grandma said, “Thank you. But I still won’t throw my old pot away. Just think about how much work it took to make this pot!”

title: Learn to Wait
summary: Patience is necessary because worthwhile things take time.
content:
Jimmy and his mother are at a restaurant. They have just ordered their food.

Jimmy begins to cry. “I am hungry! So hungry!” he cries. “Where is my food?”

His mom looks at him and says, “We only ordered our food one minute ago. It takes time to prepare and cook the food.”

Then his mom says, “Learn to wait. Good things come to those who wait.”

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?

title: Tap Tap Tap
summary: A repeated habit can become a talent and may run in a family.
content:
Tap tap tap is all Kate ever did. Sitting in school. On the bus. At home. Her tapping would drive everyone crazy.

One day her uncle bought her a set of drums. She became really good at it.

Many years passed. Kate grew up and had a son.

One day, she heard tap tap tap. It was her son. Kate smiled.

Her husband said, “Like mother, like son!”

title: A Family of Birds–1
summary: Young birds depend on their parents for care and guidance.
content:
There once was a family of birds who lived in a nest far above the canyon.

Mother and Father Bird loved their baby birds. They fed them, kept them warm, and taught them their bird song.

Tweet, tweet, tweet.

One day, Father Bird left and didn’t return. Then, Mother Bird left and didn’t return for a long time.

“Where are they?” said one baby bird.

“I’m hungry,” said another.

title: A Family of Birds–2
summary: Encouragement helps us find the courage to try something new.
content:
When Mother Bird returned, she didn’t bring enough food.

“We’re still hungry,” said the baby birds.

“Everyone, follow me,” said the mother. She flew out of the nest to the tree next door.

“Yay,” the baby birds spread their wings and flew to her. But one baby bird didn’t fly.

“Tweet, tweet, tweet,” the other birds said.

“Follow me,” Mother Bird called.

The baby bird spread his wings and finally flew to his family!

title: English and French
summary: Languages may differ, but enjoyment can be shared.
content:
When Nick visited Canada, he bought a candy bar. The label on the bar was, ‘Chocolate’ and ‘Chocolat’.

“What’s this?” Nick was puzzled.

His dad explained that Canada has two official languages. They are French and English. So, food products are labelled with both languages.

Nick ate his candy bar and said, “Chocolate is good in any language.”

options: Languages may differ, but enjoyment can be shared.

short_answer: Which country does Nick visit?

title: What Is It?
summary: Water is essential to life and many daily activities.
content:
You can see it, but you can’t hold it. It can be hot or cold. You can only live two or three days without it. Can you guess what it is?

It’s water!

We all need water. We need water to drink. We need water to cook. We need water to take a shower. We need water to grow trees, plants, and vegetables.

One person uses almost 135 litres of water every day.

Wow!

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Water is essential to life and many daily activities.

questions.prompt: What is the answer to the riddle?
How long can a person live without it according to the story?

true_false: Water can be hot or cold.
People do not need water to cook.
Plants need water to grow.

title: What’s That Smell?
summary: Animals have different ways to protect themselves from danger.
content:
One day, Sam the dog came running home. What’s that smell?

“Oh no,” said Mom. “Sam has been sprayed by a skunk.”

Skunks are small black and white animals. They do not fight with anyone. They don’t need to. But when they are scared, they make a strong-smelling liquid and spray it.

The smell makes everyone run away.

title: Changing Leaves
summary: Seasonal changes explain the beautiful colours of fall leaves.
content:
In the fall, green leaves change their colour.

The green in the leaves turns sunlight into food for the tree.

As the days get shorter and cooler, the leaves stop making food and the green fades away.

The leaves turn yellow, orange, red, purple, or brown.

Look at the pretty colours. But hurry! Soon the wind will blow the leaves away.

title: Sleeping Bear
summary: Bears prepare in advance to survive a long winter.
content:
Winter is long and cold in Canada. There is not a lot of food for the animals to eat. Black bears do not worry about that.

All summer and fall they eat. They get really fat by the time winter comes. Then, the bears go into a cave and go to sleep.

How long do they sleep? All winter long. Almost five months.

When they wake up, it is spring and, of course, they are ready to eat!

title: Not Me!
summary: Healthy daily habits can help prevent illness from spreading.
content:
Eric is five years old. He is in kindergarten.

In the middle of December, many children in his class become sick, one after another. They cough. They sneeze and they have a fever.

Their teacher says, “You’re all caught by the flu.”

But Eric isn’t one of them. Why? Eric eats well. He sleeps well. He drinks lots of water, and he washes his hands often.

The teacher says, “If we were all like Eric, the flu would not have spread.”

title: The Nile
summary: The Nile’s great length makes it an extraordinary natural feature.
content:
Do you know the longest river in Africa? It’s called the Nile. The Nile is also the longest river in the world. It is 4,184 miles long.

Crocodiles live in the Nile. They enjoy lying in the sun with other crocodiles.

Do you think a crocodile could swim from one end of the Nile to the other? It would take a very long time.
